Formulation  
The patient presents with a three-day history of a severe headache characterized by photophobia and visual disturbances, consistent with a migraine-type headache. Predisposing factors include family history of migraines (mother). The persistent nature and severity of the headache precipitated inability to work and impaired concentration. Protective factors include absence of systemic or neurological deficits, good insight, and no associated risk behaviors. No worsening systemic symptoms noted. Planned neurological examination and specialist referral will assist in further diagnosis and management.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Possible migraine headache with photophobia and visual disturbance  
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve effective symptom control to resume normal functioning and work capacity  
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm diagnosis via neurological and ophthalmologic examination; initiate appropriate migraine treatment; monitor for any complication or need to change contraceptive method  
- Actions (Patient): Book and attend scheduled neurological appointment; adhere to prescribed medication regimen, including paracetamol and stronger analgesia as advised; seek urgent care if symptoms worsen or new neurological signs develop  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange prompt neurological examination and fundoscopy; prescribe appropriate analgesia (stronger analgesic in addition to paracetamol, dose/route/frequency not documented); review blood pressure and contraceptive suitability considering migraine diagnosis; provide advice on when to seek emergency care

- Topics Covered: Migraine symptoms and management; importance of neurological examination; potential implications for contraceptive use; indications for emergency care if headache worsens or new symptoms develop  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing headache intensity, new neurological symptoms, vomiting, fever, change in vision  
- Coping Strategies: Use of prescribed analgesics; rest during peak symptoms; avoid strong light exposure
